reason: All 7 ESLint-only reports are Error(...) calls outside a throw statement (yargs-parser's error = Error(...)), which unicorn has reported since v53 (all call expressions); Biome's port (added in 1.8) checks only throw Error(...).
evidence: unicorn v53.0.0 release note 'throw-new-error: Check all call expressions instead of just argument of ThrowStatement (#2332)'; biome explain useThrowNewError: 'Require new when throwing an error'. Repro: error = Error('x') -> ESLint only; throw Error('x') -> both.

reason: All 6 Biome-only reports are typeof window / typeof self / typeof global existence checks, which unicorn stopped flagging in v66; the guarded uses are reported by both.
evidence: unicorn v66.0.0 release note 'prefer-global-this: Don't flag typeof existence checks (#3070)'; records: form-data 'typeof self === object', debug 'typeof window !== undefined', tslib 'typeof global === object'.

reason: All 6 ESLint-only arrow bodies contain a comment (// @ts-ignore, explanatory line comments, comments inside the returned object), which Biome deliberately leaves alone.
evidence: biome explain useConsistentArrowReturn: 'This rule does not report when: ... the body (or its descendants) contain comments'. Repro: (x) => { // note\n return x + 1; } -> ESLint reports, Biome not; without the comment both report.

reason: Same three lonely ifs (argparse, yargs-parser, ws): Biome reports at the else keyword and ESLint at the inner if, which is 3 to 6 lines further down because comments sit between them.
evidence: Repro: } else { followed by four comment lines and if (b) {...} -> ESLint 9:5 (if), Biome 4:11 (else); record pairs argparse 3236/3241, yargs-parser 654/657, ws 94/100.

reason: Biome reports the standard identifier-part class [$_\u200C\u200D\p{ID_Continue}] (js-tokens, path-to-regexp) as a joined character sequence although the ZWJ is followed by a property escape, not a character, so nothing is joined; ESLint reports a ZWJ only between two characters. The single ESLint-only report is an escaped combining mark (ajv), which ESLint checks by default (allowEscape: false).
evidence: Repro: /[$_\u200C\u200D\p{ID_Continue}]/u -> Biome 'A character class cannot match a joined character sequence', ESLint nothing; /[a\u200Db]/u -> both report. No Biome tracker hit.

reason: Same literal chains (whatwg-url, minimatch): ESLint reports every + between two literals and Biome one diagnostic per chain, so 'a' + 'b' + 'c' gives 2 ESLint reports and 1 Biome report.
evidence: Repro: 'ab' + 'cd' + 'ef' -> ESLint 4:16 and 4:23, Biome 4:11 only; "a" + "b" -> one each.

reason: All 4 Biome-only switches end with a // No default comment (supports-color, chalk's vendored copy, color-convert), which ESLint's default-case accepts and Biome deliberately does not support.
evidence: Biome PR #2605 (rule added), maintainer Conaclos: 'I think we should not support no default comment because we have already a suppression mechanism based on biome-ignore comments. We made the same decision for noFallthroughSwitchClause.' ESLint docs: 'You may optionally include a // no default after the last case'.

reason: The 2 Biome-only reports are cases that follow default and share its body (color-convert's default: case 6: case 0:), which Biome documents as useless while unicorn checks only cases before default; the ESLint-only report is in a line that entities suppresses with // biome-ignore lint/complexity/noUselessSwitchCase.
evidence: biome explain noUselessSwitchCase, Invalid: 'switch (foo) { default: case 0: break; case 1: break; }'. Repro: default: case 6: case 0: {...} -> Biome 2 reports, ESLint 0.

reason: The 3 Biome-only reports are feature checks through the global object (window.console.firebug, window.console.table in debug): Biome resolves window.console and globalThis.console to the console global on purpose, while ESLint's no-console only tracks references to the console variable.
evidence: Biome no_console.rs resolves the object with its global_identifier() helper (which unwraps window./globalThis. prefixes) before comparing to 'console'. Repro: window.console && window.console.table -> Biome 2 reports, ESLint none.

reason: All 3 Biome-only reports are the any-character idiom [^] (js-tokens, postcss), which Biome reports by design and ESLint lists as correct code.
evidence: biome explain noEmptyCharacterClassInRegex, Invalid: '/^a[^]/.test("ax"); // true'; ESLint no-empty-character-class, correct code: '/^abc[^]/.test("abcdefg"); // true'.

reason: ESLint reports 'Unexpected duplicate super()' for a constructor that calls super once in return super(INTERNAL).then(...) (source-map, 2 reports): its ReturnStatement handler marks the path as having called super() before the super(...) call inside the return argument exits, so the real call looks like a second one; Biome is right not to report.
evidence: Repro: class A extends B { constructor() { return super(1); } } -> ESLint 10.12.0 'Unexpected duplicate super()', Biome nothing (super(1); without return: no report). ESLint constructor-super.js ReturnStatement: 'Returning argument is a substitute of super()' sets calledInSomePaths. No ESLint tracker hit.

reason: Biome skips async arrow functions with an expression body (p-limit's (async () => function_(...arguments_))()), because the rule returns early when the body has no statement list; ESLint's require-await reports them, and Biome reports the same arrow with a block body.
evidence: Repro: const k = async (a) => a(); -> ESLint 'Async arrow function has no await expression', Biome nothing; const g = async (a) => { return a() } -> both. Biome use_await.rs run(): if query.statements()?.is_empty() { return None }. No tracker hit.

reason: Biome misses a negated test when it is parenthesized, as in json5's (propertyString !== undefined) ? propertyString : 'null'; the same ternary without parentheses is reported by both.
evidence: Repro: const x = (p !== undefined) ? p : 'null'; -> ESLint no-negated-condition reports, Biome nothing; p !== undefined ? p : 'null' -> both. No tracker hit.

reason: The one Biome-only report is semver's case '>': that ends in a /* fallthrough */ comment, which ESLint's default commentPattern accepts and Biome deliberately does not support (it relies on biome-ignore suppressions).
evidence: Biome PR #2605, maintainer Conaclos: 'We made the same decision for noFallthroughSwitchClause' (no comment-based exemption); ESLint no-fallthrough default commentPattern matches 'falls?\s?through'; semver ranges/min-version.js line 36 '/* fallthrough */'.

reason: The one ESLint-only report is the range check if (0 <= number && number < intToCharMap.length) in source-map, which Biome exempts as a range expression while ESLint's yoda reports it (exceptRange is off by default, and ESLint requires literal bounds for it anyway); note that Biome applies the exemption in if tests but not in const r = 0 <= n && n < m.
evidence: biome explain noYodaExpression: 'Range expressions like 0 < value && value < 1 or value <= 0 || 1 < value are allowed'. Repro: if (0 <= n && n < m) {} -> ESLint only; const r = 0 <= n && n < m -> both.
